report:
PASS for the two exact scoped results. The torus theorem and the exceptional-flag trapezoid are established under their retained hypotheses. This verdict does not certify arbitrary prescribed P-types, moving-model uniformity, or a general solution of original P15.3. No historical verdict or draft assertion was treated as a mathematical grant.

The torus construction works in both complex-orientation components. Each component is a connected real-analytic homogeneous manifold and a Baire space. For any nonzero integral alternating form e, the proposed basis construction produces a complex structure in the chosen component for which e(Jv₁,Jv₃)≠e(v₁,v₃): positive rescaling of v₂ preserves the orientation and can enforce this inequality. Thus the corresponding analytic type locus is proper and nowhere dense. The countable exclusion gives no nonzero integral (1,1)-classes. The coordinate two-tori generate the integral second homology of the four-torus, and translation averaging identifies their periods with the constant representative. An effective curve would have a nonzero integral (1,1)-class because its Kähler pairing is positive, so the resulting torus is curve-free.

For each nonzero lattice character, the excluded null planes consist of exactly one complex line: k(v)−ik(Jv) is a nonzero complex-linear functional. Avoiding these countably many lines gives the proposed W. The rectangular character averages tend to zero for every nonzero character; uniform approximation by trigonometric polynomials then proves equidistribution and density of every affine leaf. The rank-one form β has β²=0 and positive pairing with every Kähler form. Its class is nonzero and lies outside the divisor span.

The Liouville argument is valid for canonical subharmonic representatives, including functions with poles. Any nonzero Laplacian mass would force logarithmic growth of circular means. With zero Laplacian, the resulting bounded-above harmonic function is constant. Restricting a β-psh potential to a null leaf gives a globally subharmonic function or the identically −∞ function. A leaf through a finite point therefore has constant value c. Density and upper semicontinuity give φ≥c everywhere, making every other leaf restriction nontrivial. Comparing their constants in both directions proves φ is constant. This establishes actual potential rigidity, rather than only an almost-everywhere or measurable statement.

The descent proof genuinely applies to nonbig classes. Off the analytic exceptional image, the transferred potential is bounded above. Local smooth potentials for β reduce extension to the removability premise. The extensions glue, and pullback agrees with the original potential off an analytic subset. Equality of canonical representatives then gives equality everywhere. Bigness is unused. Consequently every retained proper bimeromorphic morphism with smooth compact Kähler source has the asserted potential rigidity and unique positive current. This argument requires no factorization of that morphism into blowups.

The numerical assertions are separate computations. Semipositivity proves nefness. Pairing a hypothetical dominating Kähler current with β, or its pullback, contradicts the zero square and positive mixed pairing, proving nonbigness. The smooth intersection degree is one. Nonpluripolar products of the smooth current are its ordinary products, so their largest nonzero cohomological degree is also one. The constant zero-potential approximation satisfies every condition in Cao’s definition, including the multiplier-ideal inclusion, and computes the same degrees. This uses Cao’s current product, not his line-bundle numerical-dimension theorem. The ordinary envelope of zero is exactly zero.

Every model curve is contracted. Its integration current pushes forward to an integral positive (1,1)-class downstairs; translation averaging and the chosen integral-type exclusion make that class zero. A nonconstant image would have positive Kähler pairing, a contradiction. The same argument applies to singular irreducible curves through their normalization. Thus the pullback class has no positive-degree curve carrier. The cutoff logarithm calculation retained in the appendix correctly constructs a small exceptional subtraction with a smooth Kähler residual, supplying a genuine blowup and smooth exceptional flag.

For each fixed model, curve Y, point q and Kähler form Ω, bounded trace mass gives sequential weak compactness of the generating currents: positivity controls all coefficient measures by their diagonal trace measures on a finite chart cover. Closedness, positivity and cohomology survive passage to the limit. If first coordinates remained bounded below by c>0 as the perturbation vanished, a subsequence would converge to the unique current β_X, while divisorial subtraction would imply β_X≥c[Y]. This contradicts the absence of curve mass in a smooth measure. Hence the supremum f(ε) tends to zero uniformly over all generating currents on that fixed model and flag.

After rational divisorial subtraction, the residual analytic potential is not identically −∞ on Y, so its positive restriction exists globally. Stokes on the curve identifies its degree with εb−tY², where b=∫YΩ. The second coordinate is an atom of this measure and therefore lies between zero and εb+|Y²|f(ε). These bounds survive closure and prove the asserted Hausdorff collapse and intersection. Smooth references are admissible gentle Kähler currents; the comparison with their zero potential is automatic from the upper bound on every compact quasi-psh potential. Thus the partial and full bodies coincide. The same compactness and curve-degree arguments apply to every stated sequence of uniformly vanishing smooth closed Kähler perturbations. They give no estimate over varying models or flags.

The conditional area assertion is also correct. For a resolved gentle current, its smooth residual B is semipositive. If A is the pulled-back smooth Kähler representative and D is the effective divisor, the difference of squared integrals is ∫D(A+B)≥0. Locality and omission of analytic sets identify the residual square with the original nonpluripolar mass. A smooth current attains the bound. Consequently the positive-level area is εA_Ω+ε²B_Ω/2. Isotropic rescaling has area tending to A_Ω, without establishing compactness or a limiting shape. Compact convex Hausdorff convergence would imply area convergence; replacing Ω by cΩ changes any such limit by √c. The reference dependence and the limited four-axiom contradiction therefore follow.

For continuation129, the small-r blowup calculation supplies an actual Kähler class K_r. The only positive-dimensional irreducible analytic subsets of the blowup are E and X itself. Along 0<r<√V, their tests are K_r·E=r and K_r²=V−r², both positive. The entire path belongs to the numerical-positivity component containing its small-r Kähler members, so the connected-component hypothesis in Demailly–Paun is established. This proves the claimed Kähler interval. Pairing any positive current of class π*[η]−bE with actual smooth representatives of K_r gives V−br≥0, hence b≤√V. The endpoint is excluded from the Kähler cone by its zero square. The assumptions a²<d and c>0 establish that Ω and every positive-level H_ε used here are Kähler.

The upper trapezoid inclusion follows from genuine current inequalities. For a generating valuation (t,y), subtraction leaves a positive current with exceptional coefficient aε+t. The preceding bound gives t≤√V_ε−aε. Its positive restriction to E has degree aε+t, so 0≤y≤aε+t. These inequalities pass to the defining closure.

The lower inclusion has the required analytic realization. For rational t and y satisfying the strict inequalities, F_t is an actual Kähler class and R=y[q]+(aε+t−y)ω_E is a Kähler curve current. Its potential has one rational logarithmic pole and a smooth remainder; degree equality gives precisely F_t|E. Deng’s complete printed extension proof applies. Its local extensions have isolated poles, are glued away from those poles, and are combined with an auxiliary divisorial potential having a rational coefficient δ. In the normalization of this problem, choose rational r>0 with y=mr and δ=nr. Near q the resulting maximum is

r log((|z₁|²+|z₂|²)^m+|z₂|^(2n))+O(1).

This is the logarithm of an actual holomorphic ideal, because the first summand is a sum of squared monomials. For y=0 the local extension is bounded instead. The extension has no generic exceptional pole and restricts to R. Adding rational t[E] preserves local rational analytic singularities and gives valuation exactly (t,y) in H_ε. The class coefficient aε need not be rational: rationality is required for the local poles, and those have been chosen rational.

These constructed currents need not themselves be gentle. DRWNXZ Lemma 3.1 is therefore essential: its locally rational analytic hypothesis is satisfied near q, and H_ε is big, so their valuation vectors belong to the closure of the gentle Kähler-current valuations. Rational points satisfying the strict inequalities are dense in the entire proposed trapezoid. Closure supplies every boundary point, without extending a non-Kähler boundary curve current. Thus the displayed region is the genuine defining body, not merely a numerical polygon.

Its four vertices and area follow directly from that body identity. Dividing the vertices by √ε gives the triangle with side length L=√(2c), area c and affine dimension two. For diagonal powers, the coordinate maxima are asymptotic to L√ε. When both exponents are below 1/2 the limit is the origin; when both equal 1/2 it is the triangle; when exactly one equals 1/2 it is the corresponding full horizontal or vertical interval of length L. An exponent above 1/2 makes the associated maximum diverge, excluding a compact global Hausdorff limit. Scaling Ω by b multiplies L by √b. The stated convergence under changes of γ and a tending to the retained data follows from convergence of these vertices.

I independently opened the version-bound primary PDFs. The complete selected printed statements and proof bodies checked include DRWNXZ’s subtraction and closure lemmas, body and partial-body definitions, and volume induction; Cao’s approximation/product definitions and comparison proof; Demailly–Paun’s Main Theorem and its connected-component proof; and Deng’s Proposition 4.16 extension proof. Demailly’s June 21, 2012 notes supply the classical removability and representative-uniqueness inputs. The primary statements in Xia and CHPW confirm the stated scope exclusions; neither supplies a theorem used in this main chain. The papers’ recursively cited foundations are distinguished from these complete selected proofs: this audit does not claim whole-work or recursive-foundation verification. Relevant primary links are [DRWNXZ v3](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2309.07584v3), [Cao v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1210.5692v1), [Demailly’s notes](https://www-fourier.univ-grenoble-alpes.fr/~demailly/manuscripts/agbook.pdf), [Demailly–Paun](https://annals.math.princeton.edu/wp-content/uploads/annals-v159-n3-p05.pdf), and [Deng v1](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1503.00112v1).

Harmless corrections: the introductory description of Deng’s input should say “Kähler curve current with finitely many logarithmic poles and smooth remainder,” rather than merely “positive analytic curve current.” The actual application already enforces this through y<aε+t. Deng’s factor-of-two potential convention must also be translated to the stated dd^c normalization; this preserves rationality and all current coefficients. Neither correction changes the argument.

Only the appendix’s indispensable blowup calculation is included in this certification. Its separate product and dense-pole constructions remain coverage/background here. The accepted results treat smooth ordinary P-type zero and the precisely stated valuation recipes; they establish no universal impossibility theorem for richer constructions.

passages.statement: On a compact Kähler manifold, every closed positive (1,1)-current T has a global representation T=θ+dd^cφ, where θ is any smooth real closed (1,1)-representative of [T] and φ is a quasi-plurisubharmonic potential. Cao, arXiv:1210.5692v1, Section 2.
passages.quote: where θ is a smooth (1, 1)-closed form

passages.statement: If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold X and v is plurisubharmonic on X minus A and locally bounded above near A, then v extends uniquely as a canonical plurisubharmonic function on X. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, June 21, 2012, Theorem I.5.24.
passages.quote: locally bounded above near A extends uniquely

passages.statement: Two canonical plurisubharmonic functions that agree almost everywhere agree everywhere; consequently the same holds for quasi-plurisubharmonic functions after adding local smooth potentials. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, Theorems I.4.18 and I.5.5.
For a positive closed (1,1)-current T, prime divisor D, and rational a≥0 with ν(T,D)≥a, T−a[D] is positive and preserves local rational analytic singularities. DRWNXZ, arXiv:2309.07584v3, Lemma 2.5.

For big ξ on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, Δ(ξ) is the compact convex closure of gentle analytic Kähler valuations, equivalently rational analytic positive-current valuations near the flag point. Gentle potentials resolve into rational effective divisor poles plus a smooth remainder. For nonbig pseudoeffective ξ, Δ(ξ)=∩ε>0Δ(ξ+ε[ω]). DRWNXZ, Definitions 2.6 and 3.2, Lemma 3.1, Section 3.

For big ξ on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, Δ(ξ) is the compact convex closure of gentle analytic Kähler valuations, equivalently rational analytic positive-current valuations near the flag point. Gentle potentials resolve into rational effective divisor poles plus a smooth remainder. For nonbig pseudoeffective ξ, Δ(ξ)=∩ε>0Δ(ξ+ε[ω]). DRWNXZ, Definitions 2.6 and 3.2, Lemma 3.1, Section 3.
For big ξ and a gentle analytic Kähler reference R∈ξ, the partial body is the closure of gentle analytic Kähler valuations satisfying T≼R. DRWNXZ, Definition 5.1.

For big ξ on a connected compact Kähler n-fold with a globally smooth connected complete flag, n!Vol_RnΔ(ξ)=vol(ξ), where vol(ξ) is the supremum of nonpluripolar top masses of gentle analytic Kähler currents in ξ. Nonbig pseudoeffective classes have volume zero. DRWNXZ, Definition 2.12 and Theorem 7.6.

For closed positive (1,1)-currents T_i=θ_i+dd^cφ_i on a compact Kähler manifold, Cao’s current product pairs a smooth closed complementary-degree form u by lim_j∫∧_i(θ_i+dd^cφ_i,j)_ac∧u, independently of the quasi-equisingular approximations. Such approximations have analytic singularities, converge in L1, have positivity errors tending to zero and monotone singularity order, and satisfy I(m(1+δ)φ_i,j)⊂I(mφ_i) eventually for every positive δ and integer m. Cao, Definitions 2–3.
passages.quote: does not depend on the choice of quasi-equisingular approximation.

passages.statement: For a compact Kähler manifold X, its Kähler cone is one connected component of the set of real (1,1)-classes α satisfying ∫Yα^dimY>0 for every positive-dimensional irreducible analytic subset Y⊂X, including X itself. Demailly–Paun, Annals of Mathematics 159 (2004), Main Theorem 0.1.
passages.quote: one of the connected components of the set P

passages.statement: Let X be a compact Kähler surface, C a smooth compact curve, F a Kähler class, and R∈F|C a Kähler current with finitely many logarithmic poles having rational coefficients and smooth local remainders. The construction in Deng’s Proposition 4.16 extends R to a Kähler current S∈F with S|C=R and rational analytic singularities near those poles when the auxiliary divisorial coefficient is chosen rational. Deng, arXiv:1503.00112v1, Proposition 4.16 and its printed proof.
